Each step starts with a 1-row light lip line (rows 1 and 16-17) and then a field of block texture, with a dark 1-row line at rows 15 and 30 as a step shadow. The steps descend away from the viewer, so only the treads are visible. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn. The view is essentially top-down, with a narrow brown cut-wall strip at the left and right edges. This matches the 'top-down slab (no front)' reference more than a front-elevation or 3/4 object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small stair block of grey treads with light edge lines and brown side strips. By eye, though, the treads read as flat grey bands with a single highlight line each. Overall it looks thinner and more sticker-like than the references, so it fails.
